pr_title: Add discontinuity support to stream recorder and fix recording on existing stream

<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the

This PR adds support for recording streams across discontinuities to go along with the HLS support across discontinuities added here in https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/46683.
This PR also addresses problems with recording when the recorder service is called on an existing stream.

Hey there @hunterjm, mind taking a look at this pull request as its been labeled with an integration (`stream`) you are listed as a [codeowner](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L450) for? Thanks!
<sub><sup>(message by CodeOwnersMention)</sup></sub>
Moved the container options up to `StreamOutput` just to avoid any problems with different options since we may end up with both types of outputs in our recorder segments.
I put this in draft because I found why it is breaking. Will think about a good fix

I think there was some change in ffmpeg which caused muxing packets twice to two different outputs to fail. I ended up making both outputs share the same StreamBuffer which probably makes more sense if we are using the same options anyway. See if it fixes the moov problems you were seeing.

Merged with dev to keep up with the rollback in https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/46684.
Ended up moving the audio codecs to `const` and just removing the video codecs. We could add back the video codecs (and the output check) if desired.
@allenporter Had to fix up some stuff after merging with the rollback. Should work now. Let me know if it works on your end.
Hmm, let me try to chase that one down. Is it when using lookback or not?

> Hmm, let me try to chase that one down. Is it when using lookback or not?

This was without using lookback.  I can do some more tests with lookback if that helps.
So lookback was explicitly set to 0 or not set at all (default)? If it was default please try again with it set to 0.

> So lookback was explicitly set to 0 or not set at all (default)? If it was default please try again with it set to 0.

I set loopback to 0 explicitly to disable it to reduce the number of possible things that could go wrong when testing since recording was not working at all before.
OK great that should be good enough. Let me try to figure it out later today or tomorrow. I'll ping you again if I find anything.

There are a couple useful standalone parts to this PR (1) keepalive streams were busted due to previous work (2) you fixed recording for nest streams (3) making discontinuity work for record

I think getting #​1 in seems like a priority that I think we should get in before more people pick up the bug.  #​2 is a great fix but not urgent, and #​3 is moving in a great direction, though may still have a problem for nest starts at startup.

Does it make sense to merge this and keep iterating on #​3? I'm comfortable with that

Or should I send you a separate PR to resolve #​1 separately since I introduced it?

See if that works. I suspect the problem was because I was basing the adjustments off the video stream, so at a boundary the audio stream might not get adjusted properly causing some packets at the boundary to overlap.

I saw a similar problem with pyav complaining about the `dts` value in a similar scenario (start of a stream, even before trying a discontinuity):
```
  File "av/error.pyx", line 336, in av.error.err_check
av.error.ValueError: [Errno 22] Invalid argument: '/tmp/snapshot_front.mp4'; last error log: [mp4] Application provided invalid, non monotonically increasing dts to muxer in stream 0: 707880 >= 555840
```
though a straight forward recording of an active stream still worked.
Wasn't able to track anything down besides the two minor changes I just pushed. You can see if they help at all, but regardless I think I'll just merge this first and work on tracking #​3 down later.

review_comments:
What is the intent of this change? I thought this was still needed to run even for recorder.

My impression is that the intent here is that "idle" callback is effectively used to end recording of the stream after duration.  That is, we have one callback per format.  The recorder never is "viewed" therefore it never keeps the idle timer awake.

Are there other bugs here?

Clarifying how this worked was my favorite part of PR #46610  I could consider ways to bring this part of the change back.
I see: keepalive is preventing this provider from being removed, and therefore you can only have one recording per stream ever? I think i'll add some tests to exercise this in a separate PR.
Yes, keepalive was preventing the recorder output from getting removed and cleaning up (running the `recorder_save_worker`)
The `recorder_save_worker` might still be running on the original deque so `clear()` might break that
